title: EKS Pod CrashLoopBackOff After Missing Secret Key
description: After a Helm release, orders-api pods restarted continuously and the rollout stalled at 1 of 4 ready replicas.
logs: Error: required environment variable PAYMENT_GATEWAY_KEY is not set
Back-off restarting failed container orders-api in pod orders-api-6c9d7f8b5-k2m4n
Container exited with code 1
root_cause: The new chart version referenced a Kubernetes Secret key (PAYMENT_GATEWAY_KEY) that had not been created in the production namespace, so the application exited at startup.
resolution: Inspect the failing pod: `kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <namespace>` and `kubectl logs <pod> -n <namespace> --previous`
Create the missing secret key in the namespace through the approved secrets workflow
Roll the deployment forward once the secret exists
Confirm all replicas are Ready
preventive_actions: Validate required env vars/secrets in CI before deploy (helm template + kubeconform + secret existence check)
Add a startup probe and a clear fail-fast error message
Use a staged rollout with automatic rollback on failed readiness

title: Payment Service OOMKilled Under Peak Traffic
description: payment-service containers were terminated repeatedly during a flash sale; checkout latency spiked and error rate exceeded 20%.
symptoms: Memory usage near the container limit before each restart
logs: Last State: Terminated Reason: OOMKilled Exit Code: 137
WARN heap usage 94% of 512Mi
kubelet: container payment-service exceeded memory limit
root_cause: The memory limit (512Mi) was too low for peak request concurrency, and an unbounded in-memory response cache grew until the kernel OOM-killed the container.
resolution: Confirm with `kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <namespace>` (Last State: OOMKilled)
Temporarily raise the memory limit/request via the normal change process
Cap or disable the in-memory cache
Scale replicas to spread load while the fix rolls out
preventive_actions: Load-test before peak events and size limits from measured p95 usage
Alert on container memory above 85% of limit
Bound all in-process caches (max entries / TTL)

title: PostgreSQL Connection Exhaustion: Too Many Connections
description: Applications began failing to open database connections; the RDS PostgreSQL instance reported it had reached max_connections after a service scaled out.
symptoms: Application errors: FATAL: sorry, too many clients already
Database CPU normal but connection count at the limit
logs: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
pg_stat_activity shows 400+ idle connections
root_cause: An autoscaling event tripled application replicas, each with a pool of 50 connections, exceeding the database max_connections of 500 while idle connections were never reclaimed.
resolution: Check connection usage: `SELECT state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY state;` (read-only)
Reduce per-replica pool size and idle timeout
Introduce PgBouncer (transaction pooling) in front of the database
Scale down replicas temporarily to restore headroom
preventive_actions: Budget connections: replicas x pool size must stay below max_connections with headroom
Alert on connection utilisation above 80%
Use a connection pooler for all services

title: Redis Cache Outage Causing Database Overload
description: An ElastiCache Redis node failed over; connections were refused for several minutes and the resulting cache misses overloaded the primary database.
symptoms: Cache hit rate dropped to near 0%
logs: redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error 111 connecting to catalog-redis:6379. Connection refused.
WARN cache miss ratio 98%
ElastiCache event: Failover from primary node complete
root_cause: A Redis primary failover left clients using stale connections; with no circuit breaker or request coalescing, every request fell through to the database (cache stampede).
resolution: Check ElastiCache events and node status in the AWS console or CLI (read-only)
Restart client connections gracefully so they resolve the new primary endpoint
Temporarily rate-limit expensive catalog endpoints
Warm the cache gradually after recovery
preventive_actions: Add circuit breakers and client retry with backoff to cache clients
Use request coalescing / stale-while-revalidate
Alert on cache hit ratio drops

title: IAM AccessDenied for EKS Service Account (IRSA)
description: Nightly report jobs failed to write to S3 after an IAM role trust policy change; pods received AccessDenied from AWS APIs.
symptoms: Jobs failing with AccessDenied on S3 PutObject
logs: botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the PutObject operation
An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity operation: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/report-generator-irsa
root_cause: A Terraform change rewrote the role trust policy with the wrong OIDC provider and service-account subject, so the pod's web-identity token was no longer trusted.
resolution: Compare the role trust policy with the cluster OIDC issuer and the service account namespace/name (read-only)
Check `kubectl describe sa <serviceaccount> -n <namespace>` for the role annotation
Correct the trust policy through the reviewed Terraform pipeline
Re-run the failed jobs
preventive_actions: Review IAM trust-policy diffs in pull requests with a second approver
Add an automated IRSA smoke test after IAM changes
Alert on spikes in AccessDenied CloudTrail events

title: NGINX Ingress 502 Bad Gateway After Backend Pod Rotation
description: Users received intermittent 502 errors during a rolling deployment; the ingress controller kept routing to terminating pods.
symptoms: Upstream connection reset in ingress logs
logs: [error] connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream
upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
Deployment web-frontend rolling update in progress
root_cause: Pods were removed from rotation before in-flight requests drained: no preStop delay and a readiness probe that lagged endpoint removal.
resolution: Verify the pattern: correlate 502 timestamps with rollout events (`kubectl rollout history deployment/<name> -n <namespace>`)
Add a preStop sleep and align terminationGracePeriodSeconds
Tune readiness probe period and maxUnavailable
preventive_actions: Standardise graceful-shutdown settings in the deployment template
Enable connection draining on load balancers
Run deployment smoke tests under load

title: Failed Production Deployment: ImagePullBackOff from Expired Registry Credentials
description: A release stalled because new pods could not pull the container image; the registry pull secret had expired.
logs: Failed to pull image "registry.example.com/notification-service:2.14.0": unauthorized: authentication required
Warning Failed kubelet ErrImagePull
Back-off pulling image
root_cause: The imagePullSecret used by the namespace held a registry token that expired the previous day.
resolution: Confirm via `kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <namespace>` events
Rotate the registry credential and update the pull secret via the secrets workflow
Retry the rollout
preventive_actions: Automate credential rotation and alert 14 days before expiry
Use cloud-native registry auth (IAM/IRSA) instead of static tokens

title: Service Timeout Cascade Due to Slow Downstream Dependency
description: Checkout latency rose from 200ms to 30s after a downstream inventory service slowed; threads were exhausted and healthy services began timing out.
logs: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out calling inventory-service
WARN executor queue full, rejecting tasks
504 Gateway Time-out upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)
root_cause: Inventory-service degraded because of an unindexed query; checkout used long default timeouts without a circuit breaker, so blocked threads cascaded the failure.
resolution: Identify the slow dependency from tracing/latency dashboards
Shed load or disable non-essential inventory calls via feature flag
Fix the slow query (add index) through the normal change process
Reduce client timeouts and enable the circuit breaker
preventive_actions: Set explicit timeouts and circuit breakers on every remote call
Add bulkheads (separate thread pools)
Load-test dependency degradation scenarios

title: Database Connection Failures After Failed Failover and DNS Caching
description: After an RDS Multi-AZ failover, applications kept connecting to the old primary IP and failed to connect for roughly 15 minutes.
symptoms: Connection refused / timeout to database host
Errors persisted after the database was healthy
logs: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: Connection to inventory-db.cluster-xyz.eu-west-1.rds.amazonaws.com:5432 refused
java.net.UnknownHostException intermittent
RDS event: Multi-AZ instance failover completed
root_cause: The JVM cached the old DNS record indefinitely (networkaddress.cache.ttl unset), so clients never resolved the new primary after failover.
resolution: Confirm failover time in RDS events and compare resolved IPs (read-only)
Perform a controlled rolling restart of affected pods
Set a short JVM DNS TTL
preventive_actions: Set networkaddress.cache.ttl to 30s or less
Include failover drills in game days
Use pool validation queries and max connection lifetime

title: EKS Node NotReady Due to Disk Pressure from Container Logs
description: Several EKS worker nodes went NotReady and pods were evicted after node disks filled with container logs and unused images.
symptoms: No space left on device errors
logs: kubelet: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage
Node condition DiskPressure=True
write /var/log/containers/app.log: no space left on device
root_cause: A debug log level left enabled in one service generated tens of GB per node; log rotation limits were not configured.
resolution: Check node conditions with `kubectl describe node <node>` (read-only)
Reduce the offending log level via config change
Cordon and drain affected nodes after confirming capacity, then recycle them
Clean unused images through the node-group lifecycle
preventive_actions: Configure container log rotation (max size / files)
Alert on node disk usage above 75%
Set ephemeral-storage requests/limits
